note.text:
Liquid–liquid mixtures:
• Immiscible liquids (they form two layers, such as palm oil and water, or kerosene and water): use a separating funnel. Let the layers settle, open the tap and run off the bottom layer; close the tap just as the top layer reaches it.
• Miscible liquids (they mix completely, such as ethanol and water): use fractional distillation. The liquid with the lower boiling point boils off first and is collected; ethanol (about 78 °C) comes over before water (100 °C).
Fractional distillation is used to get alcohol from fermented palm wine, and in industry to separate crude oil into petrol, kerosene and diesel.

worked_example.problem: Kerosene and water have been mixed by mistake. How can they be separated?
steps: Kerosene and water do not mix: they form two layers, with kerosene on top.
Pour the mixture into a separating funnel and let it settle.
Open the tap to run off the water (bottom layer); close it when the kerosene reaches the tap.

cards.idea: Immiscible liquids form layers: separate them with a separating funnel.
example: Palm oil floats on water; run the water off through the tap.

cards.idea: Miscible liquids mix completely: separate them by fractional distillation, using their different boiling points.
example: Ethanol boils at about {e} °C, water at {w} °C: ethanol comes over first.

cards.idea: Fractional distillation is also used for crude oil: petrol, kerosene and diesel boil at different temperatures.
example: The fractions are collected one after another.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for using a separating funnel in order.

items.text: Pour the mixture into the separating funnel.
Open the tap and run off the bottom layer into a beaker.
Close the tap when the top layer reaches it.
Pour the top layer out into another beaker.
